sentences.text: The warehouse operating boundary begins at the designated receiving interface and ends when a completed outbound load is released from the shipping interface.
Pallets remain within this boundary while they are inspected, identified, buffered, stored, retrieved, and prepared for dispatch.
Inbound acceptance is conditional on a valid receipt instruction and a pallet that can be safely handled within the facility.
Inbound Inspection Desk records inspection outcomes before accepted pallets enter storage operations.
Pallet Dimension Scanner captures dimensions used to determine handling and storage eligibility.
Inbound Pallet Buffer holds accepted pallets temporarily when storage work cannot proceed immediately.
Storage locations are assigned to support safe handling, efficient retrieval, and the required inventory controls.
North Aisle Stacker Crane performs assigned storage and retrieval work in its designated aisle.
South Aisle Stacker Crane performs assigned storage and retrieval work in its designated aisle.
East Transfer Conveyor carries pallets along its designated transfer route.
West Transfer Conveyor carries pallets along its designated transfer route.
Conveyor Line Controller coordinates conveyor movement within its assigned operating scope.
Autonomous Forklift Fleet moves pallets only within approved travel areas and under authorized tasking.
Yard Gate Controller controls vehicle access at the facility perimeter.
Outbound Dispatch Sorter organizes eligible pallets for their assigned dispatch sequence.
Outbound Checkweigh Scale verifies pallet weight before shipment completion.
Shipping Documentation Desk prepares the records required for outbound loads.
Warehouse Operations Supervisor oversees exceptions, operational priorities, and recovery decisions.
The Warehouse Management System, known as Morrowglass, is the authority for inventory records and the release of warehouse work.
The Warehouse Management System maintains the authoritative status, location, and handling eligibility of each controlled pallet.
No equipment may begin inventory-moving work without an authorized release from the Warehouse Management System.
Physical movement and system inventory status are reconciled so that recorded locations remain dependable throughout operations.
The service objective is to process accepted pallets accurately and meet committed dispatch times without bypassing safety or inventory controls.
Safety Zone Controller enforces movement restrictions in designated protected areas.
Fire Alarm Panel provides facility alarm status for operational response.
Maintenance Release Terminal records equipment availability for operational planning.
